newsitem.title: UK: Palm set for further falls, soft oils range bound.
newsitem.headline: Palm set for further falls, soft oils range bound.

text.p: Palm oil prices look set for further falls during the coming weeks as low exports and rising production take their toll on the market.
"The Kuala Lumpur market and project "A" tell the story for the coming week," said one trader.
The key third month on the Malaysian palm oil futures market closed at 1,182 ringgit on Friday and is expected to trade in a range between 1,170 and 1,220 in the coming week.
Strong weekly crush data issued by the U.S. National Oilseed Processors Association continued to pressure Chicago futures.
"It is going to take some very heavy orders to turn the palm oil market," said another trader.
Last week Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong forecast an increase in local palm oil output of seven percent during May over April.
Exports were project at 635,000 tonnes, but Malaysian traders said the figure needed to be near 700,000 tonnes a month to help the market.
Traders said the purchase of 25,000 tonnes of palm oil by Egypt did little for the market.
"These sort of tonnages are nothing special and the price paid was low," said one trader.
Soft oils are expected to trade within a tight range with no fresh to news to move the market in any direction.
"The market will move within limitation in line with currency and Chicago, but there is nothing fresh to move it." said one trader.
Traders said soybean and oilseed rape crops appeared to be doing well at the moment...."But it is too early for any crop scares yet," said one.
Coconut oil trading is expected to remain flat for the next two or three weeks.
"The market is stuck with nothing new fundamentally to move it, but we may see one or two major players trying to push it one way or the other depending on what suits them," said one trader.
